description: The Home Assistant link on the data plane. A hub skill sends thalovant.home.request {request_id, utterance, lang, conversation_id?}; the SDK answers each one at most once with thalovant.home.response {request_id, speech, response_type, error_code?, continue_conversation, conversation_id?}, sent as a reply (OVOS-MSG-1 §5.2): the request's context, deep-copied, with destination set to the request's source and source to the request's destination (its first entry when a list), read from the context as the hub sent it; a context with a destination and no source gets a reply with no destination at all. response_type is action_done, query_answer or error; error_code, only with error, is one of no_intent_match, no_valid_targets, failed_to_handle, unknown, timeout, agent_unavailable. A handler that raises is failed_to_handle, one that does not answer within timeout_ms (the case's own, else 9000) is timeout, one that answers with an unknown response_type or error_code is unknown -- each with speech "" unless the handler had some, since the hub speaks its own sentence for the code in the device's language. A request without a request_id is answered with request_id "". conversation_id is echoed when the handler gives none. Everything happens within the hub's bound, reply_timeout_ms (a case's hub_timeout_ms overrides it), counted from the request's arrival: the handler gets timeout_ms or what is left of the bound, whichever is less, and the reply's sending gets what the handler left; a reply that cannot be sent within the bound is withdrawn and never sent late ('deadline' cases: send_ms is how long the transport takes to send it, replied whether it went out). A reply withdrawn while it waits behind another frame -- 'queued' cases: over a real link, another frame holds the transport's send path for busy_ms from the request's arrival -- is never sent late, and withdrawing it leaves the link exactly as it was: no close, no reconnect, no error against the link (link_kept: the same link then carries another message). Only a frame already being written is finished. speech is plain text, made in this order ('speech' cases): markup is removed -- a tag is '<' or '</' immediately followed by an ASCII letter, then anything up to the next '>' outside a quoted attribute value; a comment is '<!--' to '-->'; a processing instruction '<?' to '?>'; any other '<' is text, so '5 < 6' stays -- then character references are decoded once, left to right: numeric ones (&#decimal; and &#xhex;, except 0, surrogates and anything above U+10FFFF, which stay as written), the five XML entities (& < > " ') and  , and no others; then every run of characters with the Unicode White_Space property becomes one space, and the ends are trimmed of White_Space and nothing else: U+001C..U+001F (which Python's str.strip() and Kotlin's trim() also remove), U+200B and U+180E are not White_Space and stay; U+0085 is. 'reply_context' cases check the routing alone. Every duration is whole milliseconds.
source: Home Assistant contract v1 (Wire messages); OVOS-MSG-1 §5.2; ovos-bus-client Message.reply
